Empirical Research Plan: 620‐FICO Discontinuity and the Screening Incentive of Securitizers  

-------------------------------------------------------------

1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Fuzzy Regression-Discontinuity Design (FRD) combined with a local instrumental-variables estimator.  
Rationale:  
• The probability that a loan is securitized jumps sharply (but not from 0→1) at the FICO threshold of 620, so treatment is discontinuous but not deterministic → fuzzy RDD.  
• Within a narrow band around 620 borrowers are virtually identical in observable and unobservable credit quality, so comparing outcomes just above vs. just below provides a credible counterfactual.  
• The discontinuity supplies a natural instrument (1[ FICO ≥ 620]) for actual securitization, allowing estimation of the causal effect of securitization on ex-post default.  

2. Treatment and Control  
Treatment variable: SEC_it = 1 if loan i was securitized (e.g., sold to an MBS pool within 90 days of origination).  
Running variable: FICO_it (centered) = borrower FICO – 620.  
Cut-off: 0 (i.e., FICO ≥ 620).  
Treatment group (reduced form): loans with FICO just ≥ 620.  
Control group: loans with FICO just < 620.  
Timing: treatment occurs at origination (the loan is either slated for securitization or not). Default is tracked over the life of the loan; baseline outcome = indicator that the loan ever becomes 90+ days delinquent within 24 months.  

3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
A1. Continuity of potential outcomes: Absent the securitization jump, expected default risk is a smooth function of FICO at 620. Plausible because 1- or 2-point changes in FICO reflect negligible change in underlying credit quality.  
A2. No precise manipulation of FICO around 620: FICO scores are generated by credit bureaus using proprietary algorithms, and borrowers/lenders learn the score only after data are pulled. Large-scale “gaming” of a specific integer score is unlikely. (To be tested with a McCrary density test.)  
A3. First-stage relevance: Pr(SEC=1) increases sharply at 620. Historical industry evidence and summary stats support a 20-30 pp jump.  
A4. Local exclusion: The 620 indicator affects default only through securitization, not through other abrupt changes (e.g., contract terms). We will test for discontinuities in interest rates, LTV, documentation, and other contract features; they must be smooth or controlled for.  
A5. Monotonicity (for FRD-IV): crossing 620 weakly increases the likelihood of securitization for every loan. Industry practice makes defiers implausible.  

4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation  
T1. FICO manipulation or bunching at 620.  
   • Test: McCrary (2008) density test; visual histogram.  
   • Mitigation: If slight bunching, adopt donut RDD by excluding ±1-2 FICO points; perform local randomization checks.  
T2. Simultaneous discontinuities in contract terms (e.g., higher interest spreads below 620).  
   • Test for jumps in interest rate, LTV, documentation status, broker compensation.  
   • Control flexibly for these covariates in the FRD (covariate-adjusted rdrobust).  
   • Show robustness to adding/removing controls and to alternative bandwidths.  
T3. Heterogeneous effects across lenders (e.g., some lenders always securitize).  
   • Cluster standard errors at lender level.  
   • Estimate lender-specific FRDs or include lender fixed effects; show results are not driven by any single large lender.  

5. R Code Outline (executable)  

```r
# 0. Packages ----------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)     # fast data handling
library(fixest)         # high-dimensional FE regressions
library(rdrobust)       # RDD estimation
library(rddensity)      # McCrary test
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Load data ---------------------------------------------------------
lp <- fread("LoanPerformance_2001_2006.csv")

# 2. Construct variables ----------------------------------------------
lp[, running  := FICO - 620]                      # centered running var
lp[, above620 := as.integer(running >= 0)]        # cutoff indicator

# Outcome: 90+ days delinquent within 24 months
lp[, default24 :=
      as.integer( fifelse(max_dq_24m >= 90, 1, 0) ) ]

# Treatment: securitized within 90 days
lp[, securitized := as.integer(securitization_date <= orig_date + 90)]

# Keep +/- 100 FICO points for initial bandwidth
band <- 100
sample <- lp[abs(running) <= band & !is.na(securitized) & !is.na(default24)]

# 3. Descriptive first stage ------------------------------------------
fixest::feols(securitized ~ above620 + running + I(running^2),
              data = sample, cluster = ~lender_id)

# 4. Main FRD estimation (local linear, MSE-optimal bandwidth) ---------
frd <- rdrobust(y = sample$default24,
                x = sample$running,
                fuzzy = sample$securitized,
                covs = cbind(sample$LTV, sample$lowdoc, sample$int_rate),
                p = 1)   # local linear
print(summary(frd))

# 5. Robustness: alternative bandwidth & donut ------------------------
# (a) Donut: drop loans within 2 FICO points of cutoff
donut <- sample[abs(running) > 2]
frd_donut <- rdrobust(y = donut$default24,
                      x = donut$running,
                      fuzzy = donut$securitized)
summary(frd_donut)

# (b) Placebo cutoffs
placebo_scores <- c(600, 640)        # just examples
results_placebo <- lapply(placebo_scores, function(cut){
  dat <- lp[abs(FICO - cut) <= band]
  rdrobust(y = dat$default24,
           x = dat$FICO - cut,
           fuzzy = dat$securitized)
})

# 6. Density test ------------------------------------------------------
dens <- rddensity(sample$running)
summary(dens); plot(dens)

```

6. Expected Results  
Theory predicts securitization weakens lender screening, so the local average treatment effect of securitization on default should be positive. Based on industry default rates (~15-20 % 90-day delinquency in subprime cohorts), I expect a 2–4 percentage-point increase (≈15–25 % relative) for loans marginally eligible for easy securitization.  

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment for FRD (1 = satisfied, 0 = questionable)  
C1. No manipulation of running variable: 1 (will confirm via density test)  
C2. Continuity of baseline covariates at cutoff: 1 (test and show)  
C3. Large, sharp first stage: 1 (historical evidence ≥20 pp jump)  
C4. Local average treatment interpretation appropriate: 1 (monotonicity believable)  
C5. Robustness to bandwidth and polynomial choice: 1 (multiple bandwidths & donut/placebo checks)  

Total: 5/5 – identification appears strong, subject to empirical confirmation.
